caption: The drawing depicts a wooden structure resembling a confessional booth, positioned on a hexagonal tiled floor with large reddish and beige tiles. The booth is primarily golden brown with intricate decorative details and ornate patterns including rectangles, diamonds, and oval shapes. Some panels feature carved motifs or reliefs, with darker accents highlighting the designs. The upper central section has a curved, arched canopy adorned with turned finial posts on top. A cushioned black armrest or headrest is situated inside the arch. The booth sits against a wall partially covered by a dark gray curtain hanging from a rod that stretches horizontally above and to the side of the booth. The curtain appears heavy and creates an enclosed space around the booth. A small rectangular door with a latch is visible inside the structure. The overall color palette consists mainly of yellows, browns, grays, and black, with the floor providing subtle contrast in warm earth tones.
title: Side of Confessional Chair
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
